title: Jet missing for 13 years found in an Ozark cave
summary: A post made to look like a Branson, Missouri, TV news report claimed a jet that vanished in 2013 with 212 people aboard was found inside an Ozark Mountains cave. Lead Stories found the story started on a Facebook satire page, and Google's SynthID detector flagged the image as made with AI.
tell: The "news station" is a page whose own bio says it is satire, and no real outlet reported the find.

title: Prince Harry shoving Meghan outside Buckingham Palace
summary: A viral video claimed to show Prince Harry shoving Meghan Markle while holding their daughter outside Buckingham Palace. Lead Stories found signs of AI throughout and no reports of any such incident from established news outlets.
tell: Watch the hands and car door: they warp and melt into each other, and the child seems to float with nothing holding her.

title: Map of lead fallout from the Iowa Army plant blast
summary: A map shared on X claimed to show where lead dust would fall after the Army's planned detonation at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. Lead Stories found it was a snowfall forecast from a college weather-model site and matched neither the Army's maps nor one AP published.
tell: The map's own title says it shows snowfall, and NAM is a NOAA weather model, not a military one.

title: Huge waves flooding Gordon's Bay, South Africa
summary: A video shared on Threads claimed to show powerful waves surging over the beachfront at Gordon's Bay, South Africa. Lead Stories found it was made with AI, and an earlier TikTok copy carried an AI-generated label.
tell: Look closely: cars sit on top of houses, no people are around, and the flooded buildings show no damage.

title: Giant sea worm rising behind a cruise ship
summary: A video on X claimed to show an enormous worm-like creature rising from the ocean behind a cruise ship. Lead Stories found AI detection tools rated it very likely AI-made, and no news outlet reported any such sighting.
tell: The creature looks like the sandworm from the movie Dune, and a news search turns up no reports of it.

title: Malcolm in the Middle stars buying GTA in 2013 and 2026
summary: Two photos shared on X claimed to show actors Bryan Cranston and Erik Per Sullivan buying Grand Theft Auto in 2013 and again buying GTA VI in 2026. Lead Stories found both pictures were made with AI, and detection tools found Google's AI watermark in them.
tell: Check the ages: Sullivan was born in 1991, yet the 2013 picture shows a child and the 2026 one shows a teenager.

title: Woman on a treadmill falling out a gym window
summary: A TikTok video presented as new showed a woman on a malfunctioning treadmill falling out of a gym window, with the gym ordered to pay a large fine. Lead Stories found it was made with AI from one frame of security footage of a real 2024 accident in Indonesia, and the details in the narration don't match the real case.
tell: Look at the background: some people in the clip are frozen like equipment, and a treadmill shakes while nothing above it moves.

title: Government memo warning about an iPhone update
summary: An image shared online claimed to be a Homeland Security Investigations memo saying an iOS 27 update secretly listens to nearby conversations and sends them to Apple for ads. Lead Stories found the memo was not real, and several AI detectors flagged the image as AI-made.
tell: A scary official-looking memo that only shows up as a screenshot, with no agency or Apple announcement behind it, deserves doubt.

title: Rockstar letter delaying GTA VI to 2027
summary: An Instagram post shared what looked like a Rockstar Games letter saying Grand Theft Auto VI was pushed back a full year to November 2027. Lead Stories found no such announcement from Rockstar or any major news outlet, and the post itself was tagged as ragebait.
tell: A delay this big would be on the company's own news page and everywhere in the news, not just one social post.

title: Sabrina Carpenter and co-stars in a Palantir ad
summary: A post claimed a photo of Sabrina Carpenter, Margaret Qualley and Madelyn Cline was an ad for the tech company Palantir. Lead Stories found it was a behind-the-scenes still from a Carpenter music video, edited to add Palantir branding, and posted by an account that calls itself satire.
tell: Check the posting account's bio: this one says all its posts are satire.

title: A nationwide 90-day blackout starting Nov. 17
summary: TikTok posts, one using an edited clip of the president, claimed a 90-day nationwide blackout would start Nov. 17. PolitiFact rated it false: the clip was doctored, and what is actually planned that day is a national Emergency Alert System test on TV and radio.
tell: No agency announced a blackout, and urgent warnings with no named official source are a red flag.

title: King Charles's "urgent address" about his son
summary: A website story claimed King Charles III gave a tearful emergency address about a tragedy involving his son, with a photo of him crying. Lead Stories found no such speech on the royal family's site or in the news, and detection tools flagged the photo as AI-made.
tell: Read past the headline: the story's own text admits there's no verified evidence the address happened.
